definitions.explanation: The entrance area of a Japanese home or building where visitors are received and shoes are removed. A transitional space between outside and inside.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{脱|ぬ}いでください→脱ぐ：00518_nugu⟧。
examples.english: Please take off your shoes at the entrance.

examples.japanese: {玄関|げんかん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ベル→ベル：01379_beru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{鳴|な}りました→鳴る：01143_naru⟧。
{玄関|げんかん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}りました→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: I decorated the entrance with flowers.

notes:
{玄関|げんかん} is the entrance area of a Japanese building, culturally significant as the boundary between inside and outside.

Components:
- ⟦{上|あ}がり{框|かまち}→上がり框：10774_agarigamachi⟧ (step up into the house)
- ⟦{土間|どま}→土間：07849_doma⟧/⟦たたき→三和土：10765_tataki⟧ (earthen floor/concrete area)
- ⟦{下駄箱|げたばこ}→下駄箱：06490_getabako⟧ (shoe cabinet)
- ⟦{傘立|かさた}て→傘立て：07013_kasatate⟧ (umbrella stand)

Cultural aspects:
- Shoes are removed before stepping up
- The lowered floor keeps dirt from entering
- Often has ⟦{表札|ひょうさつ}→表札：04886_hyousatsu⟧ (nameplate) outside
- Guests may be greeted but not invited further (⟦{玄関先|げんかんさき}→玄関先：noentry⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧)

Expressions:
- {玄関|げんかん}⟦{払|ばら}い→払い：09655_barai⟧ - turning someone away at the door
- ⟦{玄関先|げんかんさき}→玄関先：noentry⟧ - at the entrance (without inviting in)
